data.title: Phosphorylation of TRAIP is essential for mitotic replisome disassembly and MiDAS
data.projectDescription: Chemical cross-linking coupled to mass spectrometry was used to study the structure and homodimerization of the E3 ubiquitin ligase TRAIP from Xenopus laevis. The protein was cross-linked with two different concentrations of disuccinimidyl suberate (DSS).
data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Cross-linking was performed according to previously described procedures (Leitner et al., Nat. Protoc., 2014) with two DSS concentrations, 0.1 and 0.33 mM. Cross-linked samples were digested in solution using endoproteinase Lys-C and trypsin. LC-MS/MS analysis was performed by data-dependent acquisition on a Thermo Orbitrap Fusion Lumos mass spectrometer.  Further information can be found in the accompanying publication.
data.dataProcessingProtocol: MS/MS spectra were searched using xQuest/xProphet (Walzthoeni et al., Nat. Methods, 2012), version 2.1.5, against the sequences of the target protein (including tags) and identified contaminants/copurified proteins from the E. coli expression system (the database in fasta format is provided). Important xQuest search settings were as follows: Enzyme = trypsin, maximum number of missed cleavages = 2, MS mass tolerance = 15 ppm, MS/MS mass tolerance = 15 ppm. Reactive sites for DSS were K and the protein N terminus.  The false discovery rate was controlled by searching against reversed sequences. Due to the small number of target identifications, an accurate estimation of false discovery rates is difficult. However, no decoy hit remained after filtering and manual evaluation of the spectra. Raw files ending in …01 and …02 correspond to the 0.1 mM DSS condition, while …04 and …05 correspond to the 0.33 mM DSS condition. Further information can be found in the accompanying publication.
